messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed on gw-prod ingress. 5m error-rate = 4.2% (baseline ~0.3%). Affected routes: /v1/generate (high QPS), /v1/embeddings. Pager -> @oncall-manager.

alice-nguyen: I'm looking. Jumping into traces and logs. Initial glance: very few spans for the failing requests — traces either not sampled or not ingested.

ben-ortega: I can take a handoff in ~10m if needed. @oncall-manager ping me when you hand off.

carla-lee: Quick check: log ingestion (logstash -> ES) is returning backpressure errors and rejecting some payloads. Also seeing KV-cache warnings about metadata size. Might explain missing trace/log correlation.

devon: Ingress (envoy) is emitting a lot of 504 upstream_timeouts with no request-id header present in many of those requests. If request-id missing we can't stitch traces. There was a KV-cache PR yesterday that trims headers — could be related.

alice-nguyen: I'm going to enable 100% trace sampling for gw-prod for the next 15m and bump log verbosity. Need to patch the deployment.

alice-nguyen: Applying patch now:
```
kubectl set env deploy/gw-prod TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0 LOG_LEVEL=debug -n infra
kubectl rollout restart deploy/gw-prod -n infra
```

sre-bot: Rollout started for deploy/gw-prod. build=bld-2026-345. Estimated restart 45s/pod.

ben-ortega: Taking handoff now from @alice-nguyen. @alice drop links to traces/logs when they start coming in.

alice-nguyen: After restart we see traces again, but a lot of spans are flagged as "unindexed" in the trace backend. Logstash is rejecting messages with "metadata too large" errors. Looks like metadata size is causing ingestion failures.

carla-lee: I can apply a low-risk stopgap at logstash to drop specific heavy metadata keys. Patch to add to pipeline:
```
if [metadata][kv] {
  mutate { remove_field => ["[metadata][kv][heavy_field_1]", "[metadata][kv][heavy_field_2]"] }
}
```
I'll roll that in with a small canary.

devon: I'll add a tiny envoy lua filter to inject a compact request id header (x-rid) when x-request-id is missing so we at least have a short correlation key even if full metadata is trimmed.

devon: Envoy snippet (concept):
```
-- lua
local rid = req:headers():get("x-request-id") or short_uuid()
req:headers():add("x-rid", rid)
```

ben-ortega: Applying both patches (logstash filter + envoy x-rid injection) to gw-prod and rolling in. Monitoring.

sre-bot: Dashboards update: error-rate fell to ~2.1% after the first pods came back online. Continuing to watch.

alice-nguyen: We're still seeing a concentrated set of failures in eu-west-1. Digging into backend shard metrics — shard-3 showing connection pool exhaustion and leak indicators. This explains persistent 502s for a subset of traffic.

alice-nguyen: For immediate mitigation I'm going to route /v1/generate traffic in eu-west-1 to the backup pool. Command:
```
redwood-routing set-weight --route /v1/generate --region eu-west-1 --to gw-backup=100
```

oncall-manager: Please record customer impact details (affected endpoints, percent of traffic, ETA for mitigation) and whether requests are retry-safe.

ben-ortega: Quick triage: roughly 6% of /v1/generate requests in eu-west-1 saw 502s between T-10 and now. No data loss expected (requests are idempotent). Recommend posting a brief status page note and emailing top 5 customers in the region. Assigning @carla-lee to draft the message.

carla-lee: Draft status update: "We are investigating elevated 5xx rates affecting text generation in eu-west-1. Traffic has been rerouted to a backup pool and temporary tracing/log fixes applied. No data loss expected; mitigation in progress." Will post and notify.

alice-nguyen: With metadata trimming + x-rid injection + 100% sampling we now have full spans for the failing flows. Root cause appears to be: the KV cache change introduced a large session blob (~50KB) into request metadata that pushed spans over the tracing index size limit, causing traces to be marked unindexed and log pipeline to reject messages. Secondary problem: a connection leak in backend shard-3 causing exhaustion under burst.

devon: Immediate next steps: rollback the KV-cache metadata change in the next release and patch shard-3 connection pooling. For stopgap we have:
1) Route eu-west-1 traffic to backup pool
2) Logstash metadata trim filter
3) Inject x-rid header at ingress
4) 100% tracing for 30m (then scale down)

ben-ortega: I'll keep monitoring and will scale sampling back after 30m unless needed. Also filing an alert for trace-ingest-errors > 1% to catch this earlier.

sre-bot: Ticket INF-4523 created to follow up on KV-cache PR, connection leak fix, and improved pipeline alerting. Tagged: @alice-nguyen, @devon, @carla-lee.

oncall-manager: Handoff to ben-ortega complete. Escalate if the backup pool shows issues.

ben-ortega: Current quick metrics: 5m error-rate trending down to ~0.6%, trace ingestion success ~98%, log pipeline errors dropped to near-zero after trim. Will update in 15m.

alice-nguyen: Post-incident notes: three observability gaps contributed to slower diagnosis — missing request-ids, oversized metadata causing unindexed traces, and log ingestion backpressure. Stopgap instrumentation (x-rid, metadata trimming, 100% sampling) restored visibility and enabled the targeted mitigation (routing + backend fix). Follow-ups: enforce metadata size cap (pre-commit lint), add CI check for KV-cache PRs that modify metadata payload, and add alerting for logstash rejects and trace-index errors.

carla-lee: Status page update posted and top 5 customers emailed.

ben-ortega: Monitoring looks stable. I'll keep the channel open for 30m and then close if no regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Ticket INF-4523 logged. Incident marked as under active mitigation; future postmortem to be authored once follow-ups complete. :white_check_mark:
